_comment: Every (platform, surface, coordinate) triple where an installed datrix.platforms plugin
has NOT declared a decision that another installed platform HAS declared -- the seven
capability surfaces the block-realization parity gate checks (block cells, secret
backends, observability providers per category, deployment runtimes, identity
(provider_type, feature) cells, scalar capability fields, unrealizable_surfaces).
This is a DELIBERATELY MAINTAINED SCOPE BOUNDARY, not an auto-heal: every entry is a real,
reviewed gap in a platform's PlatformCapabilityDeclaration, catalogued here so the gate can
run green while the underlying gap is fixed on its own schedule. Removing an entry means the
platform's declaration was updated to cover that coordinate -- do it in the same change that
edits the declaration.
expected_count is a pinned, reviewed value: change it only in the same change that adds or
removes an entry.
coordinate format is surface-specific: 'block_type:flavor' for block_realizations,
the bare enum .value for supported_secret_backends/supported_runtimes,
'category:provider_value' for native_observability_providers,
'provider_type:feature' for identity_feature_realizations,
the bare field name (or 'scalar:<field>' union-value coordinate) for a scalar surface,
the bare surface_name for unrealizable_surfaces.
Surface 5 (identity_feature_realizations) carries the largest share of entries: each
platform declares full feature coverage only for the identity provider type(s) it can
actually host (aws->cognito, azure->entra-id/entra-external-id, docker/local->zitadel);
'external' (client wiring to a pre-existing IdP) is declared symmetrically by all three,
so it contributes zero entries here. This is real, previously-uncatalogued platform state,
not a gate artifact.
